note_tweet.text:
So let me get this straight.

19 people (including a 7 year old) got crushed to death at a Durga Puja festival in India because, *checks notes* it started raining?!

People outside rushed into the shelters for cover. People already inside refused to leave because they didn’t want to get wet (surprise surprise)

Narrow exits, basically zero crowd control, and some genius blaring over the sound system that the structure was about to collapse

Result? A full on stampede...

Per the BBC, a senior police official said the “commotion” kicked off after the rain and the announcements. Crowd starts “pushing, pulling, and rushing forward” and people go down...

And this isn’t some random freak accident. Stampedes at Indian religious festivals are basically a seasonal event at this point.

9 dead last November on Ekadashi

30 dead in January at the Kumbh Mela while 10,000+ people tried to bathe in the "sacred river"

115 crushed or drowned in 2013 at a temple in Madhya Pradesh after a rumor that the bridge would collapse made everyone collapse the bridge🤦‍♂️

Most of these barely even make international news because it happens so often. At some point you gotta start looking at contributing factors.

I'm sure a pattern or two will emerge.
